title: Daily life: in progress, done, not yet
title_target: កំពុង ហើយ នៅឡើយ — kam-pung, haeuy, neuw-laeuy
goal: Talk about your daily routine — and use ហើយ correctly, because it is not an "already" you can stick on anywhere.
bekal: tell the story of a day, from waking up to going to bed
use កំពុង for actions in progress
use ហើយ for finished actions and changes of state
answer the question … ហើយឬនៅ?
say how often with រាល់ថ្ងៃ, ជួនកាល, មិនដែល

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Breakfast before work
dialogs.intro: Sokha and Ani meet outside the house early in the morning. Watch the three little words that run this whole conversation: កំពុង, ហើយ, and នៅ. The verbs themselves never change form, not even once.

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [អរុណសួស្ដី|'a-run sua-sdey] [បង|baang]! [ក្រោក|kraok] [ពី|pii] [ដេក|dék] [ហើយ|haeuy] [ឬនៅ|reu-neuw]?
lines.id: Good morning! Are you up yet?
lines.literal: morning-good — older-sibling! rise — from — sleep — already — or-not-yet?

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ក្រោក|kraok] [ហើយ|haeuy] [ចាស|chaah]។ [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ក្រោក|kraok] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប្រាំ|pram] [រាល់ថ្ងៃ|roal-thngay]។
lines.id: Yes. I get up at five every day.
lines.literal: rise — already — yes(f). I — rise — o'clock — five — every-day.

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: ព្រឹក [ណាស់|nah]! [ញ៉ាំ|nyam] [បាយ|baay] [ហើយ|haeuy] [ឬនៅ|reu-neuw] [បាទ|baat]?
lines.id: That's early! Have you eaten yet?
lines.literal: morning — very! eat — rice — already — or-not-yet — yes(m)?

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [នៅ|neuw] [ទេ|té] [ចាស|chaah]។ [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [កំពុង|kam-pung] [ដាំ|dam] [ទឹក|teuk]។
lines.literal: not-yet — no — yes(f). I — in-the-middle-of — boil — water.

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [ម្តាយ|mdaay] [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ធ្វើ|thweu] [បបរ|baa-baa] [ហើយ|haeuy] [បាទ|baat]។ [មក|mòòk] [ញ៉ាំ|nyam] [ជាមួយ|chiè-muèy] [យើង|yeung] [ទៅ|teuw]។
lines.id: My mother has made rice porridge. Come and eat with us.
lines.literal: mother — I — make — porridge — already — yes(m). come — eat — with — us — go-on.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: អរគុណ [ចាស|chaah]! [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ត្រូវ|treuw] [ចេញ|cheñ] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប្រាំពីរ|pram-pil] [ចាស|chaah]។ [ទាន់|toan] [ទេ|té]?
lines.id: Thank you! I have to leave at seven. Will I make it?
lines.literal: thank-you — yes(f)! I — must — go-out — o'clock — five-two — yes(f). in-time — (question)?

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [ទាន់|toan] [បាទ|baat]។ [ឥឡូវ|'ey-leuw] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប្រាំមួយ|pram-muèy] [កន្លះ|kan-lah] [ទេ|té]។
lines.id: You'll make it. It's only half past six now.
lines.literal: in-time — yes(m). now — o'clock — five-one — half — only.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [បង|baang] [ធ្វើការ|thweu-kaa] [រាល់ថ្ងៃ|roal-thngay] [ទេ|té] [ចាស|chaah]?

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [អត់ទេ|'at-té]។ [ថ្ងៃ|thngay] [អាទិត្យ|'aa-tit] [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [សម្រាក|sam-raak]។ [ជួនកាល|chuèn-kaal] [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ទៅ|teuw] [វត្ត|woat]។
lines.id: No. On Sundays I rest. Sometimes I go to the wat.
lines.literal: no. day — sun — I — rest. sometimes — I — go — wat.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [បង|baang] [ដេក|dék] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប៉ុន្មាន|pon-maan] [ចាស|chaah]?
lines.id: What time do you go to bed?

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប្រាំបួន|pram-buèn] [ឬ|reu] [ដប់|dop] [បាទ|baat]។ [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [មិនដែល|min-dael] [ដេក|dék] [យប់ជ្រៅ|yup-chreuw] [ទេ|té]។
lines.id: Nine or ten. I never stay up late.
lines.literal: o'clock — five-four — or — ten — yes(m). I — never — sleep — night-deep — no.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ត្រូវ|treuw] [រៀន|rien] [ពី|pii] [បង|baang] [ចាស|chaah]!
lines.literal: I — must — learn — from — older-sibling — yes(f)!

grammars.title: កំពុង, ហើយ, នៅ — three words that replace a whole verb table
body: Khmer never changes a verb to show time. ដេក stays ដេក for "sleep", "is sleeping", "has slept", and "will sleep". These three little words do that job instead.
after: កំពុង and នៅ are very close in meaning, and Cambodians often swap them without any problem. The difference is subtle: **កំពុង stresses that the action is happening now**, **នៅ stresses that it hasn't stopped yet**. At A1, using កំពុង for both will never be misunderstood.

grammars.title: ⚠️ ហើយ is not an "already" you can stick on anywhere
body: Learners tend to attach ហើយ everywhere, thinking it simply means "already". In fact ហើយ marks a **change of state** — something that wasn't so before is so now. That is why it also appears in sentences where English would never say "already".

head: Khmer
Say it
Translation
What changed
rows: ម៉ោងប៉ុន្មានហើយ?

after: Look at rows four and five. ម៉ោងប៉ុន្មានហើយ? uses ហើយ even though English doesn't say "what time already?" — because for Khmer, time is a state that keeps changing.

⚠️ Don't use ហើយ for habits or durations alone. "I've worked here for a long time" is not ខ្ញុំធ្វើការទីនេះហើយ. For how long, use បាន + length of time: ខ្ញុំធ្វើការទីនេះបានពីរឆ្នាំហើយ ("I work here, have got two years now").

grammars.title: … ហើយឬនៅ? — the question you'll hear most
body: "Already or not yet?" is the most common question pattern in Khmer, and its answers follow a fixed pattern worth memorizing whole.

head: Question
"Yes, already" answer
"Not yet" answer
rows: ញ៉ាំបាយហើយឬនៅ?
នៅទេ / មិនទាន់ទេ
មិនទាន់ដល់ទេ

after: ⚠️ A "not yet" answer **never** uses ហើយ. And as usual, you answer by repeating the verb, not by saying "yes" or "no". ញ៉ាំបាយហើយឬនៅ? ("Have you eaten yet?") is also an everyday greeting, much like "How are you?" — so don't be surprised if your neighbor asks it three times a day.

blocks.text: ⚠️ These frequency words can go **at the start or at the end** of the sentence without changing the meaning: រាល់ថ្ងៃខ្ញុំក្រោកម៉ោងប្រាំ and ខ្ញុំក្រោកម៉ោងប្រាំរាល់ថ្ងៃ are both correct. The only one you can't move is មិនដែល, which must sit right before the verb.
